Yea I kept it somewhat vague, which is how it was before in the timer part of the spec that deals with activation/deactivation.

I thought of exposing "document activated/deactivated" in the HTML spec, which would be somewhat implementation specific in terms of when it's called to begin with, and do the following (similar to your proposed algorithm)

- For each timer, save the "Earliest expiry time" as a timestamp rather than an "estimate callback time" method.
- On a reversible deactivation (as in, "can be reactivated", or not unload/BF), save the deactivation time.
- On reactivation, check the difference between now and the deactivation time, and add that difference to each of the document's window's active timers' earliest expiry time.
- While we're at it, dispatch `visibilitychange` upon activation/deactivation.

I thought to postpone it to a later patch, but I don't mind condensing them to one.
WDYT?

OK, I think the new version makes this a lot more explicit in terms of "fully active".

The only (standard) occasion when a timer can update its expiry time based on activity is in the BFCache case, where a `salvageable` document who is not `fully active` maintains its list of active timers alive in case it's salvaged.

I updated the BFCache-related algorithms to assign a "suspension timestamp" and "list of suspended timer handles" to the document, which would have their expiry timestamps updated upon resume (navigate to an existing `document` salvaged from history).
